title: THE COURTYARD AND THE OPEN GATE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Set up the courtyard around it and put the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard.'" - Exod 40:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One short instruction closes the layout: a boundary, and a doorway in it.

Both matter. The courtyard curtain marked out what belonged to God — this space is set apart. The entrance curtain marked the way in — and you may come.

God's people have often struggled to hold those two together. Some emphasise the boundary until the faith looks like a fortress with no visible door. Others emphasise the welcome until nothing is set apart at all and there is no distinct life to be welcomed into.

The tabernacle had both, and neither cancelled the other.

Jesus embodied this perfectly. He was utterly holy, and He ate with tax collectors and sinners (Luke 15:1-2). No compromise, no distance.

Our lives should have the same shape. Clear lines about how we live, held with genuine warmth toward everyone outside them. Paul put it simply: be wise in the way you act towards outsiders, letting your conversation be full of grace, seasoned with salt (Col 4:5-6).

A boundary without a door is a prison. A door without a boundary leads nowhere in particular.

Build both.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is your faith more fortress or more open field?
2. Do people know both what you stand for and that they are welcome?
3. Who could you invite in this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me clear lines and an open door. Let my life be set apart and welcoming at the same time. Amen.
